subject: Phased fulfillment proposal: OEM lead times + cloud backfill coordination
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@hyperoem.com>, GCP Sales <gcp-sales@cloudcorp.com>, John Dwyer <j.dwyer@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Phased fulfillment proposal: OEM lead times + cloud backfill coordination

Team / partners —

Quick summary: ACME needs a dedicated pool sized for their Peak-100 workloads for launch in Q4. OEMs are quoting ~14–18 week lead times for the initial GPU tranche, while cloud backfill is available sooner but at higher unit cost. To protect the launch timeline we want to propose a phased fulfillment plan that blends OEM physical delivery with cloud-reserved capacity as a backstop.

Ask: Alicia / HyperOEM — can you confirm the following from your side by EOD Wed: (1) firm earliest ship week for the 120-unit tranche if we sign PO by 30 Jun, (2) ability to split delivery into two shipments (40 units immediate, 80 units T+12 weeks), and (3) any lane-specific constraints (SKUs that ship later / require specific rack orders).

GCP Sales — please share an explicit backfill offer (regional availability, per-GPU hourly and monthly committed pricing, and a limited-run SLA for the Q4 ramp) so we can model blended unit costs and an acceptance window for cloud fallback.

Internal next steps (Karthik / Ben / Monica): I want a cost / latency tradeoff sheet and a suggested tranche schedule by Thu so we can present to ACME and attach a preferred PO cadence.

Attachments: none in this note; Alicia, feel free to attach the latest quote PDF.

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

From: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@hyperoem.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, John Dwyer <j.dwyer@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Phased fulfillment proposal: OEM lead times + cloud backfill coordination

Hi Vivek / John / Karthik —

Thanks for the clear ask. Quick answers and clarifications below, followed by an attached formal quote.

1) Earliest ship week: If PO and deposit are received by 30 Jun we can ship the first 40-unit tranche week of 2026-10-04 (approximately 14 weeks) assuming no customs delays. The remaining 80 units target week of 2026-12-13 (approx. 24 weeks) if we stage a second production slot; alternatively we can target T+12 with an expedited premium if you confirm materials lane availability now.

2) Split deliveries: Yes — we can split into 40 / 80 but there are two caveats: (a) split creates an additional freight and test-handling charge (~$12k tranche), and (b) the later tranche is susceptible to SKU allocation changes if higher-priority OEM bookings occur in the interim. We can hold SKUs for 30 days post-PO; beyond that we recommend a binding deposit schedule.

3) Lane constraints: The A100-6144 variant ships at full cadence; the denser FP16-optimized SKU has a constrained fab lane (estimated +6 weeks on the second tranche). Recommend substituting to the A100-6144 across both tranches for predictability, or accept potential variance.

Attachment: [Attachment: HyperOEM_quote_v2.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]

If helpful I can produce a variant with binding deposit milestones and penalty clauses — ping me and I’ll get legal to draft.

Best,
Alicia Ramos
Strategic Accounts – HyperOEM
[Phone redacted]

From: GCP Sales <gcp-sales@cloudcorp.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, John Dwyer <j.dwyer@acmecorp.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Phased fulfillment proposal: OEM lead times + cloud backfill coordination

Hi Vivek / team —

Thanks for the heads-up. We can offer a regional reserved node fleet in us-west1 on a 3-month term to cover up to 120 GPUs within 2–3 weeks of contract execution. Two pricing options attached: (A) short-term committed reserve (higher hourly) and (B) 3-month commit with discount. Both include network and monitoring and an SLA for availability during the reservation window.

Notes: (1) We prefer to be the near-term backfill rather than long-term due to unit economics; (2) cross-region replication required for redundancy will add additional egress costs; (3) onshore support for ACME can be included with a 10% uplift.

Attachment: [Attachment: Cloud_Backfill_Terms.docx (DOCX, 24KB)]

If you want I can provision a soft-reservation (non-billable) to lock capacity while legal and finance complete contract paperwork — that holds for 10 business days.

Regards,
Cloud Solutions Team
CloudCorp

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@hyperoem.com>, GCP Sales <gcp-sales@cloudcorp.com>, John Dwyer <j.dwyer@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 11:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Phased fulfillment proposal: OEM lead times + cloud backfill coordination

Thanks all — synthesized plan and action items below (internal callouts + items for external partners).

SYNTHESIS:
- Requirement: ACME needs 120 GPUs for Peak-100 model serving by early Dec; strong preference for physically owned capacity for unit economics long-term but launch timing is critical.
- Recommended tranche schedule (proposal):
  * Tranche A (Immediate backfill): 40 GPUs (cloud reserved) provisioned mid-Jul to cover initial staging & alpha.
  * Tranche B (OEM short ship): 40 GPUs — HyperOEM ship target week 2026-10-04.
  * Tranche C (OEM final): 40 GPUs — second OEM shipment (or expedited T+12 with premium) to reach full 120 by early Dec.

COST / RISK NOTES:
- Blended unit economics: Cloud backfill per-GPU effective monthly $ higher by ~28% vs OEM capex amortized over 36 months; but cloud avoids launch slippage risk.
- Contingency: If HyperOEM second tranche slips >8 weeks, we recommend exercising an accelerated cloud conversion for that tranche and negotiate a partial credit against OEM deliverables.

ACTION ITEMS:
- Vivek / Ben: finalize PO terms with deposit schedule by Mon 29 Jun. Include clause: 30-day SKU hold on tranche allocation + penalty matrix for >30 day attrition.
- Alicia: provide deposit-variant quote with explicit freight/test charges line-items (requested by EOD Fri).
- CloudCorp: provision soft-reservation to lock 40 GPUs in us-west1 for 10 business days and share formal 3-month pricing matrix.
- Monica: model blended-costs + latency map for ACME’s regional traffic and surface to John for sign-off.

John — can you confirm ACME’s tolerance for blended-costs vs launch date sensitivity? A single-line reply here is fine (we’ll use that as gating for finance sign-off).

Thanks —
Karthik
Director, Capacity & Onboarding, Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@hyperoem.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, GCP Sales <gcp-sales@cloudcorp.com>, John Dwyer <j.dwyer@acmecorp.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Phased fulfillment proposal: OEM lead times + cloud backfill coordination

Vivek / team —

Confirming receipt and alignment. I attached the deposit-variant quote as requested and added the freight/test charge line. We can hold the SKU allocation for 30 days after PO; if you elect a 2-stage binding deposit schedule we can extend hold to 90 days and guarantee tranche timing (subject to force majeure).

We will accept a 20% deposit to lock Tranche B (40 units) and an optional 10% forwarding deposit to hold Tranche C skus. We’ll mark the expedited path pricing in the quote.

Attachment: [Attachment: HyperOEM_quote_v2.pdf (revised) (PDF, 49KB)]

Please confirm PO issuance timeline so I can push production scheduling internally.

Best,
Alicia Ramos
Strategic Accounts – HyperOEM
